slides.name: 1 · Partnership Pack

params.text: Research, hackathons and programmes tackling the social problems technology keeps missing.

slides.notes: The deck follows the written pack. Before it goes anywhere: set the real costs, and fill in the bracketed confirmations — particularly the Sickle Cell outcomes, which the pack itself calls the strongest proof point with no numbers attached.

slides.name: 2 · What the Institute is

params.text: A lot of technology gets built for a narrow slice of the population, and the consequences land hardest on communities that were never in the room.
Puts those communities in the room — alongside clinicians, data scientists, engineers and academics, on problems that matter to them.
The research and programme arm of UK Black Tech. Where the parent builds the ecosystem, the Institute produces the evidence, the training and the prototypes.

slides.notes: Three beats: the problem, the method, the relationship to the parent. The third matters commercially — a partner who wants brand reach across a tech community wants the UK Black Tech pack, not this one, and saying so early saves a wasted meeting.

slides.name: 3 · What we have built so far

params.text: What we have built so far
Digital courses created with Tech Mums, FutureLearn and the University of Leeds.
The Sickle Cell Hackathon — doctors, data scientists, patients and web developers, at the Design Museum.
Including a collaboration with LSBU’s Computer Science department.

slides.notes: Track record, not ambition. Keep it to things that have finished.

slides.name: 4 · The Sickle Cell Hackathon

params.text: The UK’s most common genetic blood disorder, disproportionately affecting people of African and Caribbean heritage — and chronically under-served by health technology.
Patients in the build process alongside the clinicians treating them and the developers who could prototype. From the first hour, not as a consultation at the end.
It is the clearest example of how the Institute works, and it is the thing partners ask about.

slides.notes: THIS SLIDE NEEDS NUMBERS. The pack says so itself: participants, prototypes produced, what happened to them afterwards, press coverage, continued development. It is the strongest proof point in the pack and it currently has none attached. A partner will ask, and "I would have to check" is a worse answer than a modest real figure.

slides.name: 5 · The research agenda

params.text: Women’s Health in the Age of Technology
how digital health tools serve, or fail to serve, women and particularly Black women
where datasets under-represent communities, and what that produces downstream

slides.notes:
Two real themes and two to fill in. Do not present the placeholders — either add the themes or cut the rows, because an agenda that is half blank reads as an agenda that is half imagined.

The pack also asks for published outputs, working papers and studies in progress. A partner funding research wants to see what your research actually looks like before they fund more of it.

slides.name: 6 · Why partner with the Institute

params.text: Recruitment into health research from Black and minority communities is a known, documented problem. We have earned the trust to do it — as partners with those communities, not extractors of data.
Hackathons produce prototypes. Courses produce trained people. Reports are written to be used.
Clinicians, patients, academics and engineers in one room is harder to arrange than it sounds. It is most of what we do.
Specific, evidenced and defensible — including under Social Value Model requirements in public procurement.

slides.notes: The fourth one closes deals with procurement teams and nobody else. Know which of the four the person in front of you is buying.

slides.name: 7 · Section · Partners fund our work. Partners do not determine our findings.

params.text:
Partners fund our work.
Partners do not determine our findings.

slides.notes:
The most important slide in the deck and the one to slow right down on. It is on the green because it is the thing you want the room to look up at.

The argument, if it is challenged: a report a sponsor could have edited is a marketing document, and everyone reading it knows that. Independence is not a constraint on the value — it is the value.

slides.name: 8 · What that means in practice

params.text: Methodology, analysis and conclusions sit with the Institute and its academic collaborators.
Partners see findings before publication and may correct factual errors about their own organisation. They may not require changes to conclusions.
In the published output, every time.
Including when it is inconvenient to a funder.

slides.notes: Five rules, revealed one at a time. This is standard practice for a credible research institute — say that, because it reframes the terms from awkward to professional.

slides.name: 9 · Partnership routes · placeholder costs

params.data:
Route	Scope	Placeholder cost
Research	Insight brief	£15,000
Research	Full study	£45,000
Research	Multi-year programme	£100,000+
Programme	Course development	from £20,000
Programme	Cohort delivery	from £12,000
Hackathon	Lead partner	£30,000
Hackathon	Supporting partner	£10,000

slides.notes:
PLACEHOLDER COSTS, and research scope varies enormously — treat these as the shape of the offer, not the number. Set your own before this goes to a partner and change the title when you do.

There is no description column: with one, every row wrapped to two or three lines and the last two rows fell off the bottom of the slide. Seven routes and a price is what a table on a wall can carry. The detail is for saying, not showing — an insight brief is desk research plus a community survey with a launch webinar; a full study adds primary fieldwork, academic collaboration, a launch event and media outreach at around forty pages; the multi-year programme runs two to three years with annual outputs. Lead hackathon partners co-define the challenge and take a named, full participating role; supporting partners get presence, mentor places and prize sponsorship.

Also available and not on the slide: in-kind hackathon support — venue, technical mentors, compute credits, clinical expertise — valued case by case. And learner bursaries at £500 a head, which needs your actual per-learner cost.

slides.name: 10 · Institute Partner · the annual route

params.text: 12 months. One insight brief, supporting hackathon role, observer status, five volunteering places.
24 months. One full study, lead on a hackathon each year, one course, advisory board observer, fifteen places.
36 months. Two or more studies, lead plus challenge-setting, two courses and a bursary fund, full board seat, unlimited places.

slides.notes: For organisations wanting a sustained relationship across all three strands rather than one commission. Every figure is a placeholder. All three include being named on Institute outputs, early access to findings, and an annual impact report written for your own reporting.

slides.name: 11 · What partnership does not buy

params.text:
Editorial control over findings.
Exclusive or embargoed access to data beyond the agreed pre-publication window.
Endorsement of your products or services by the Institute.
Use of community participant data for commercial purposes.
Association with our community without a genuine contribution to it.

slides.notes:
Stated plainly so there are no difficult conversations later. It reads as confidence rather than as restriction when it comes straight after the independence slide, which is why it sits here and not at the end.

And the one that costs nothing: universities, NHS trusts, patient organisations and charities are not charged to collaborate. Those relationships run on shared contribution — access, expertise, data, ethics approval, co-authorship, venue.

slides.name: 12 · How it works

params.text: Six steps, and ethics before fieldwork
What you need to achieve, what we are already working on, and whether there is a genuine overlap. We will say so if there is not.
Scope, method, timeline, cost, outputs — and the independence terms restated in full.
Contract signed. Where research involves human participants, ethics approval is secured through our academic partner before any fieldwork begins.
With agreed checkpoints. You will know if timelines move, and why.
Joint launch event, media outreach, output published openly.
In a format that goes straight into your CSR, ESG or social value reporting.

slides.notes: Step three is the one that separates this from a marketing engagement. Do not rush past it.
